scope: All original 1,298 lexical headwords, parts of speech, genders, and meanings read; all actual pronunciation meanings compared; three new homographs and fixes rechecked. Every grouped form checked mechanically against the complete 38-master corpus route inventory, with independent contextual checks of diagnosed cases.
limitations: This review reuses the course source audits and exact lesson evidence. It is not a fresh paleographic collation of every source form. Machine coverage does not alone establish sense correctness.

accepted_oe_entry_projection.method: SHA256 of UTF-8 JSON of old_english_entries only, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, compact separators

accepted_hash_rebind.reason: Visual review caught a rebuild regression dropping 11 reviewed past participles and negative present nis. All 13 reference-ledger records, including already-present forloren, have now been verified in both entry data and master prose; polarity form-ID checks have zero errors. The final self meaning, self; the same person or thing, matches the registered sense and its four U08 evidence routes.
accepted_hash_rebind.linguistic_scope: OE master, complete form lookup, and the OE-entry projection. The full entries.json hash records this snapshot but does not freeze or review later English-only route edits.

findings.finding: Pronunciation spellings earm, full, and weax matched unrelated existing lexemes; arm, adjective full, and wax needed their own senses and routes.
findings.resolution: Separate noun earm, adjective full, and noun weax entries and exact lookup routes verified; existing adjective/adverb/verb entries preserved.

findings.finding: Conventional labels for defective modals were printed without the register citation caveat.
findings.resolution: All four now state conventional citation label and no usable infinitive supplied.

findings.finding: Positive and negative principal diagnostics were combined without polarity labels.
findings.resolution: Display labels now separated. Any remaining positive/negative form-ID mixing is enumerated in diagnostic_form_id_repairs.

findings.finding: Different register analysis schemas hid past participle citations and one explicitly parsed negative present diagnostic.
findings.resolution: All unambiguous semantic-schema base participles now present. The reviewed remaining exact records are enumerated in diagnostic_repairs; positional reference rows were checked individually against ch16 table.

findings.finding: Generic nominal diagnostics on verbs mixed present/past participles, strong/weak inflections, and genders under bare genitive singular or nominative plural labels.
findings.resolution: Suppressed from ordinary verb diagnostics; all actual forms remain in grouped Forms lists. Verified zero such diagnostics.

findings.finding: Technical ID geliefan-permit leaked into the learner headword through the inherited register display_headword.
findings.resolution: Exact supplied headword gelīefst, pres. ind. 2 sg., with permission/dative usage; no unevidenced citation inferred.

findings.finding: Inherited unmarked ungecnawen was used as a headword although the exact source predicate is ungecnāwen.
findings.resolution: Headword now ungecnāwen, explicitly labelled past participle; supplied predicate.

findings.finding: Supplied inflected ethnic names benefit from their exact source case labels so no learner infers an unprovided nominal paradigm.
findings.resolution: Exact labels and source routes are enumerated in source_name_label_proposals.

findings.finding: An early reviewer suspicion that Apollines was genitive was wrong.
findings.resolution: Apollines is the source nominative name-form for Apollo, distinct from Apollonius. Current headword and sense are valid; do not introduce a genitive label.

findings.finding: The correction appendix initially printed audit imperatives and omitted the actual weak-verb meaning, leaving the valid-word/source-error distinction incomplete.
findings.resolution: Exact learner wording, reward cross-reference, and personally rechecked Main30b evidence are recorded in appendix_repairs. This stays a correction notice, outside ordinary paradigm forms.

appendix_repairs.proposed_note: Weak verb: sin; fail in duty. Cook 34.9 erroneously gives this as a hint for reward; see āgyldan (strong III), whose contracted third singular is āgylt. C06 preserves and corrects the original hint.
appendix_repairs.image_inspection: Reviewer personally viewed Main30b. Entry a-gyltan, -giltan gives weak gylte/gilte and gylt/gilt, fail in duty / become guilty / offend / sin against; distinct a-gyldan has geald/guldon/golden and repayment senses.
appendix_repairs.verified_in: glossaries/old-english.md, rendered correction notice; the form lookup retains its original audit note as provenance
